config.title: Generics — Types as Parameters

intro.title: Generics — Types as Parameters
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, reusable identity function that returns whatever input it receives. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics to treat types as parameters, making your code flexible and type-safe. The main constructs involved are generic functions and type parameters, which allow you to write components that work with a variety of data types. This beginner-friendly introduction will help you understand how to avoid repetitive code while maintaining strong type checking.
intro.usecase: Generics are essential for building reusable UI components in TypeScript applications, such as data tables, dropdowns, or form inputs that need to work with various data types. For example, a dashboard might use a generic `<DataTable<T>>` component to display user profiles, financial transactions, or product inventories while maintaining strict type safety for each column. This pattern allows developers to write a single, flexible component that can be adapted across different features, like filtering panels or modal content, without sacrificing compile-time error checking. Mastering generics enables you to create scalable, maintainable codebases where components are both versatile and type-safe.

objectives: Implement generic functions that accept type parameters
Construct generic interfaces to define flexible data structures
Apply generic constraints to limit acceptable type arguments
Initialize generic classes with multiple type parameters
Manipulate arrays using generic utility types
Configure generic type aliases for reusable type definitions
Integrate generics with existing TypeScript type systems

steps.title: Import TypeScript and React

steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React is imported and ready to use with TypeScript.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing React from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Please import React from 'react'.

steps.title: Create a generic identity function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'identity' that uses a generic type parameter and returns its input unchanged.
steps.hint: Use the syntax <T> before the parameter list. The function should take one argument of type T and return the same type.
steps.seedCode:
import React from 'react';

// Define your generic identity function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A generic function 'identity' is defined and ready to be used with any type.
successCriteria: The 'identity' function is defined with a generic type parameter <T>, takes one argument of type T, and returns type T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function uses a generic type parameter <T> and returns the same type it receives.
steps.feedbackWrong: Not quite. The function should be named 'identity', use a generic type parameter <T>, take one argument of type T, and return type T.

steps.title: Add type parameter to identity function
steps.instruction: In the identity function, add a type parameter <T> to the function signature.
steps.hint: Add <T> right after the function name to make it generic.
steps.expectedOutcome: The identity function signature includes a type parameter <T>.
successCriteria: The identity function is declared with a type parameter <T> in its signature.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to add <T> right after the function name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature should include a type parameter, like <T>, to make it generic.

steps.title: Use the generic function with different types
steps.instruction: Inside your identity function, add a type parameter T and make the function return the input value with proper typing.
steps.hint: Add <T> before the parameter list and annotate the parameter and return type as T.
steps.expectedOutcome: The identity function will be properly typed with a generic type parameter T.
successCriteria: The identity function has a type parameter T, accepts a parameter of type T, and returns type T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the type parameter <T> and properly typed both the parameter and return type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The identity function should have a type parameter <T> and return the input value with type T.

steps.title: Create a generic interface
steps.instruction: Define a generic interface named 'Container' with a single type parameter 'T' and a property 'value' of type T.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name, type parameter in angle brackets, and the property definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: A generic interface named Container with type parameter T and property value: T.
successCriteria: The Container interface is defined with a type parameter T and property value of type T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface has both the type parameter 'T' and the 'value' property with type T.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create an interface named Container with a type parameter T and a property called value of type T.

steps.title: Implement the generic interface
steps.instruction: Create an object named 'stringBox' that implements the generic interface with type parameter 'string'.
steps.hint: Use the interface name followed by type annotation and assign an object with a 'value' property of type string.
steps.expectedOutcome: An object named 'stringBox' is created that implements the generic interface with the string type.
successCriteria: It uses the generic interface with type parameter 'string'
It has a 'value' property of type string
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your object is named 'stringBox' and implements the generic interface with type parameter 'string'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The object doesn't properly implement the generic interface. Check that you're using the correct interface name and type parameter.

steps.title: Create a generic React component
steps.instruction: Create a functional React component named 'GenericDisplay' that accepts a generic type parameter for its props. The component should return a simple <div> element.
steps.hint: Define a component with a generic type parameter in angle brackets after the component name, similar to how you defined the identity function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A generic React component named GenericDisplay is defined with a type parameter and returns a <div> element.
successCriteria: The component GenericDisplay is defined with a generic type parameter and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component has a generic type parameter and returns JSX (like a <div>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a component named GenericDisplay with a generic type parameter that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize component state with generic type
steps.instruction: Inside your generic React component, initialize a state variable using useState with a generic type parameter that matches the component's type parameter.
steps.hint: Use the same type parameter T from your component in the useState hook call.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable that uses the generic type parameter T.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with a generic type parameter T, and the state variable is properly typed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the generic type parameter T with useState and properly typing the state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the generic type parameter T with useState to create type-safe state.

steps.title: Define handler functions with generic types
steps.instruction: Inside your GenericComponent, define a handler function called 'updateState' that takes a value of type T and updates the component's state with it.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts a parameter with type T and calls the setState function with that value.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your GenericComponent will have a handler function that can update the state with type-safe values.
successCriteria: The GenericComponent contains an 'updateState' function that accepts a parameter of type T and calls the state setter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your handler function accepts a parameter of type T and properly updates the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function is missing or doesn't properly handle the generic type T. Try creating a function that takes a value of type T and updates the state.

steps.title: Render the component with type-safe markup
steps.instruction: Inside the GenericComponent function, return JSX that displays the current state value and includes a button to update it with a new value.
steps.hint: The JSX should include a paragraph showing the current state value and a button with an onClick handler that calls your update handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render with type-safe markup that displays and allows interaction with the generic state.
successCriteria: The GenericComponent returns JSX containing a paragraph displaying the state value and a button with an onClick handler that updates the state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your JSX includes both a paragraph showing the state value and a button with an onClick handler that calls your update function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet return the required JSX. Remember to include a paragraph displaying the state value and a button to update it.
